title: Nachshon Enters the Sea
text:
The book of Exodus tells how the Israelites, fleeing Egypt, were trapped between the sea and Pharaoh's approaching army, and how the waters parted before them. The rabbis of the Talmud asked a question the Bible does not answer: who went into the water first?

Rabbi Meir taught that the tribes competed for the honor and the tribe of Benjamin jumped in first. Rabbi Yehuda told it differently. Each tribe, he said, held back and said it would not be the first to go into the sea. Then Nachshon, the son of Aminadav and prince of the tribe of Judah, stepped forward and walked into the water, and his tribe followed him.

At that moment, in Rabbi Yehuda's telling, Moses was standing in long prayer. God told him that this was no time for long prayers, while His beloved ones were drowning in the sea. Later midrashic tradition adds that Nachshon kept walking until the water reached his nose, and only then did the sea split.

The Talmud says that because of this act, the tribe of Judah was given royal leadership in Israel.
lesson: Some situations will not change until someone commits before the way is clear. Leadership often means being the first to step in while everyone else waits to see what happens.
people: Nachshon ben Aminadav, the tribe of Judah, Moses
source: Babylonian Talmud, Sotah 36b to 37a; Mekhilta de-Rabbi Ishmael, Beshallach
caveat: This is a rabbinic legend that expands the biblical account, and the rabbis themselves recorded competing versions.
